bear_case.title: China dominates cells
bear_case.description: In grid storage (ESS) specifically, CATL shipped 125.0 GWh in H1 2026 (+81% YoY) for a 27.1% overall share, with BYD fourth at 35.7 GWh (7.7% share); in EV batteries the two hold a combined 54.3% of global shipments. North America/Europe/other now account for 56% of ESS shipment destinations for the first time — geographic diversification is real, but manufacturing scale still sits overwhelmingly with Chinese cell makers.

bear_case.title: Policy whiplash is already claiming casualties
bear_case.description: Section 301 duties on non-EV lithium-ion (grid BESS) cells jumped from 7.5% to 25% effective Jan 1, 2026, pushing the effective combined US import tariff on Chinese ESS batteries to ~58.4%; new FEOC rules cap Chinese-sourced content at 45% of manufacturing cost for ITC eligibility. Wood Mackenzie now projects the US utility-scale storage market could contract 11–29% in 2026 on this policy uncertainty, and integrator Powin's Chapter 11 liquidation (assets sold to FlexGen) is a concrete example of a tariff-driven casualty.

bear_case.title: Margin compression
bear_case.description: Fluence's Q3 FY26 print is the freshest evidence: GAAP gross margin fell to 5.1% from 14.8% on contract-manufacturing delays, with $400M of deliveries now slipping into FY27 — on top of Tesla's own Q2 energy-segment margin nearly halving (39.5% → 20.4%) and Eos Energy's gross margin still near -69%. Software attach (Stem's 55% non-GAAP gross margin) remains the differentiator; hardware stays under real pressure from Chinese cost structures.

bear_case.title: Solid-state timelines
bear_case.description: QuantumScape's Eagle Line pilot is producing and the Honda pact holds, but there's still no production license or volume commitment; 2026 adjusted EBITDA-loss guidance remains $250–275M and shares are down more than 50% YTD, underscoring how far off meaningful revenue still is.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.note: Backlog $176B en route to $200B by 2027, plus a new Blue Energy hybrid gas+SMR 2.5GW Texas plant and a Joulent/Microsoft data-center power deal, reinforce the grid-equipment bottleneck thesis — this is the physical scarcity trade, not a storage-cell trade. Overlaps your Nuclear sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Megapack 3 began production at the Brookshire, TX Megafactory in early August — 16 months from groundbreaking, 28% more energy per unit, and 1 GWh deployable in 20 business days via Megablock. The ramp thesis is now shipping product, not just a construction timeline. Overlaps your Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Fluence Energy
positions.note: Shares stabilized (+3.6% Aug 11 to $13.10) and Citi upgraded to Buy ($24 PT) even as Morgan Stanley and RBC cut targets to $15 after the $400M FY27 delivery slip; still watching for the gross-margin path to actually recover before sizing a position.

positions.name: Eos Energy
positions.note: Q2 revenue $68.8M (+351% YoY) and a record $807M backlog were reinforced by a new Golden Dome defense contract diversifying Z3 zinc storage beyond utility customers, but a -$1.20 EPS miss and gross margin still near -69% (plus dilution from the $150M rights offering) keep this small and speculative.

positions.name: QuantumScape
positions.note: Eagle Line pilot output continues (yield/uptime/cost now the focus) and the Honda R&D pact holds, but there's still no production license, no volume commitment and no revenue — the long wait continues.

positions.name: Enphase
positions.note: A 6% pop on US AI-focused power-electronics manufacturing (IQ Solid-State Transformer) and a new Italy full-home launch are real product wins, but they don't fix the structural US residential-solar policy headwind behind the segment's revenue decline.

positions.name: Stem Inc
positions.note: Q2 marked a fifth straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA (+63% YoY to $6.2M), a record 55% non-GAAP gross margin and operating cash flow at breakeven — real profitability progress even as revenue keeps shrinking YoY; still not sized, but no longer a clear avoid.

positions.name: Energy Vault Holdings
positions.note: The 1.25GW Texas data-center BESS deal (~$500–600M of expected 2H26–2027 revenue) is a legitimate proof point, but it's one deal from one developer — want to see it repeat before sizing a position.
